intro: Jacksonville routed Baltimore on Thursday night to extend its lead in the AFC South, and Minnesota will start Carson Wentz on Monday night with Kyler Murray sidelined. The winless Chargers host Houston, and Cincinnati and Atlanta fly to Madrid for Sunday morning. 160 stories across all 32 teams.

top.label: Biggest Story
top.headline: Jaguars rout Ravens 33-10 on Thursday night
top.dek: Jacksonville moved to 6-2 and leads the AFC South by three and a half games. Baltimore played without Lamar Jackson and fell to 4-5.

top.label: Injury Watch
top.headline: Kyler Murray out, Wentz to start for Vikings Monday
top.dek: Murray's hamstring strain ends a run of five straight games where he took every snap. Safety Theo Jackson missed Thursday's practice, and left tackle Christian Darrisaw is expected to practice.

top.label: Player Spotlight
top.headline: Josh Allen passes Jim Kelly for Bills TD record
top.dek: Allen threw for 289 yards and two scores against Baltimore and ran for another. His fourth-quarter touchdown to DJ Moore was career pass number 259, one more than Kelly.

top.label: Stat of the Day
top.headline: 27: drives since the Chargers last scored a touchdown
top.dek: Los Angeles has gone nine quarters without a touchdown and sits at 0-7. No team that started 0-7 or worse has made the playoffs.

top.label: What's Next
top.headline: Bengals and Falcons meet in Madrid on Sunday morning
top.dek: Cincinnati plays Atlanta at Bernabeu Stadium on Sunday at 9:30 a.m. ET on NFL Network. Watch the Bengals secondary against Atlanta's passing game.

teams.name: Buffalo Bills
teams.headline: Bills prep for Vikings blitz after 36-10 rout

stories.text: Bills turn to Vikings blitz plan after routing Ravens
stories.summary: Buffalo sits at 6-1 after a 36-10 win over Baltimore and now faces a 6-1 Minnesota team on Monday night. Practice this week centers on protection adjustments and quick decisions from Josh Allen against a defense that sends extra rushers. The Bills' offense is confident, but how it handles pressure will shape the game.

stories.text: DJ Moore and Spencer Brown top Bills' injury list
stories.summary: Wednesday's report listed receivers DJ Moore (knee and shoulder) and Joshua Palmer (hamstring) and tackle Spencer Brown (back), all with status to be determined. Defensive tackle Greg Gaines (calf) and cornerback Dee Alford (ankle) sat out the Ravens game. Sources disagree on how Moore's Week 8 ended, so watch Friday's report.

stories.text: Josh Allen passes Jim Kelly for most TD passes in team history
stories.summary: Allen went 21 of 34 for 289 yards and two touchdowns against Baltimore, plus a rushing score on the opening drive. His fourth-quarter touchdown to DJ Moore was career pass number 259, one more than Kelly for the franchise record.

stories.text: 19: Tyler Bass sets a Bills record with straight field goals
stories.summary: Bass made a 56-yarder against the Ravens for his 19th consecutive field goal, a franchise best. He is also the first Bills kicker with seven straight makes from 50 yards or longer.

stories.text: Bills visit Vikings on Monday night
stories.summary: Buffalo plays at Minnesota on Monday, Nov. 9 at 8:15 p.m. ET on ESPN, with both teams at 6-1. Watch how the Bills protect Allen against the Vikings' blitz packages.

teams.name: Miami Dolphins
teams.headline: Dolphins squander 13-3 halftime lead vs Patriots

stories.text: Dolphins let a 13-3 halftime lead slip against New England
stories.summary: Miami led the Patriots at the break and lost 24-19 as New England scored 21 straight second-half points. Coach Jeff Hafley called the first half the team's best of the year and the finish a teaching moment. The Dolphins are 1-6.

stories.text: Jaylen Wright upgraded as Dolphins practice shorthanded
stories.summary: Running back Jaylen Wright (quad) missed Wednesday and moved to limited on Thursday. Guard Kadyn Proctor cleared concussion protocol and practiced fully, and quarterback Malik Willis (groin) was full both days. Eight other Dolphins were limited on Thursday, and running back De'Von Achane is out for the season with a torn ACL.

stories.text: Chop Robinson keeps rushing the passer for Miami
stories.summary: Robinson sacked Drake Maye twice against New England, and NextGen Stats has him leading all pass rushers in pressure rate this season. He also answered Hafley's challenge to repeat his Week 4 performance at Minnesota. He is on the injury report with a knee issue, listed as limited.

stories.text: 21: unanswered points Miami allowed after halftime
stories.summary: The Patriots outscored the Dolphins 21-3 after the break, hitting touchdown throws of 43 and 48 yards as the secondary broke down for a second straight week. Miami held Maye to 53 passing yards in the first half.

stories.text: Lions visit Hard Rock Stadium on Sunday
stories.summary: Miami hosts Detroit on Sunday, Nov. 8 at 1 p.m. ET on CBS. The Lions are 5-2. The Dolphins are 0-3 at home this season.

teams.name: New England Patriots
teams.headline: Patriots rally in the rain to beat Miami

stories.text: Patriots rally past Dolphins 24-19 in the Miami rain
stories.summary: New England trailed 13-3 at halftime and won on the road behind 21 unanswered points. Mike Vrabel pointed to quarterback Drake Maye's leadership as the difference. The Patriots are 5-3 and host Green Bay on Sunday.

stories.text: A.J. Brown, Hunter Henry sit out Wednesday practice
stories.summary: Receiver A.J. Brown (ankle and knee), tight end Hunter Henry (foot), tackle Christian Barmore (illness) and running back TreVeyon Henderson (illness) did not practice Wednesday. Quarterback Drake Maye (shoulder) was a full participant. Safety Kevin Byard, cornerback Carlton Davis and edge rusher Gabe Jacas were among seven limited players.

stories.text: Drake Maye accounts for three more touchdowns
stories.summary: Maye hit 16 of 20 passes for 199 yards and two touchdowns, ran in another, and committed no turnovers. He completed all nine throws to wide receivers for 156 yards. Kyle Williams and DeMario Douglas each caught a touchdown of 40 yards or more.

stories.text: 5: straight games with three touchdowns for Maye
stories.summary: Maye has produced at least three total touchdowns in five consecutive games, the longest Patriots streak since Tom Brady's 10-game run in 2007. He averaged 7.4 yards per play in the second half against Miami, up from 3.5 in the first.

stories.text: Packers visit Foxborough on Sunday afternoon
stories.summary: New England hosts Green Bay on Sunday, Nov. 8 at 4:25 p.m. ET on FOX, with both teams at 5-3. Watch whether Brown and Henry return to a thin receiving group.

teams.name: New York Jets
teams.headline: Jets seek first win in four at Kansas City

stories.text: Jets drop third straight one-score game, 38-33 to Raiders
stories.summary: New York scored a season-high 33 points and still lost after Geno Smith threw a game-ending interception to Jeremy Chinn. The Jets are 2-6 and have lost three in a row. They now travel to face a 5-2 Chiefs team.

stories.text: Garrett Wilson in concussion protocol, Breece Hall full
stories.summary: Wilson did not practice Wednesday or Thursday while in the concussion protocol. Running back Breece Hall was a full participant Thursday for the first time since his quad injury, and tight end Mason Taylor and edge rusher David Bailey also went full. Defensive lineman Harrison Phillips (ankle) did not practice.

stories.text: Braelon Allen runs for 147 yards in Hall's absence
stories.summary: Allen carried 21 times for 147 yards and a touchdown against Las Vegas, starting in place of the injured Hall. He has topped 100 scrimmage yards in four straight games. His 504 rushing yards since Week 4 rank second in the league.

stories.text: 504: Braelon Allen's rushing yards since Week 4
stories.summary: Only Tampa Bay's Bucky Irving has more rushing yards over that span. Six Jets have reached 100 yards in a game this season, the most for the franchise since 2010.

stories.text: Jets visit Chiefs at Arrowhead on Sunday
stories.summary: New York plays at Kansas City on Sunday, Nov. 8 at 1 p.m. ET on CBS. The Chiefs are 5-2 but coming off two straight losses. Watch whether Hall returns to share the load with Allen.

teams.name: Baltimore Ravens
teams.headline: Jaguars rout Ravens 33-10, fourth straight loss

stories.text: Ravens fall to 4-5 as Jaguars roll on Thursday night
stories.summary: Jacksonville beat Baltimore 33-10 in the rain, and the Ravens have now lost four straight after a 4-1 start. Rookie Joe Fagnano made his first start and went 10 of 18 for 60 yards with two interceptions. Parker Washington's 50-yard touchdown just before halftime put the Jaguars up 17-3 at the break.

stories.text: Lamar Jackson to injured reserve; Hamilton hurts hip
stories.summary: Jackson went on injured reserve with a right thumb injury and will not return soon. Safety Kyle Hamilton left in the third quarter with a hip injury and did not come back, and no update was available. Cornerback Nate Wiggins sat out with an illness, and Fagnano played with a heavily wrapped ankle.

stories.text: Derrick Henry climbs to seventh on the all-time rushing list
stories.summary: Henry carried 17 times for 57 yards and passed LaDainian Tomlinson for seventh place on the NFL's career rushing list. He also took 10 direct snaps at quarterback. Justice Hill added a 65-yard touchdown run in the fourth quarter, Baltimore's first second-half touchdown since Week 5.

stories.text: 4: straight games under 14 points, a first in Ravens history
stories.summary: Baltimore has scored fewer than 14 points in four consecutive games, a first for the franchise. It also lost three straight by at least 20 points for the first time. Four false starts on Thursday pushed the Ravens' league-high pre-snap penalty total to 24.

stories.text: Chargers visit Baltimore on Monday Night Football
stories.summary: The Ravens host the Los Angeles Chargers on Monday, Nov. 16 at 8:15 p.m. ET on ESPN at M&T Bank Stadium. Baltimore is 4-5 and still needs to settle its quarterback spot with Jackson on injured reserve. Watch the offense's early-down execution and the false starts.

teams.name: Cincinnati Bengals
teams.headline: Bengals head to Madrid riding Burrow's hot streak

stories.text: Bengals fly to Madrid at 5-2 after 43-36 overtime win
stories.summary: Cincinnati beat Tennessee 43-36 in overtime in Week 8 and now travels to Atlanta for the NFL's Madrid game. Joe Burrow threw for 462 yards and accounted for six touchdowns against the Titans. The offense has scored 78 points over its last six quarters.

stories.text: Turner, Johnson and Dugger miss practice before Madrid
stories.summary: Defensive back DJ Turner (heel), defensive end Cedric Johnson (ankle/foot) and safety Kyle Dugger (quad) did not practice, and Jordan Battle (hamstring) was limited. Zac Taylor called Turner and Johnson day to day. Rookie Cashius Howell is on injured reserve and will miss the game.

stories.text: Tee Higgins earns AFC Offensive Player of the Week
stories.summary: Higgins caught 10 passes for 155 yards against the Titans and took home AFC Offensive Player of the Week honors. Ja'Marr Chase added 11 catches for 141 yards in the same game. The pair gave Burrow two 100-yard targets in one overtime shootout.

stories.text: 752: Burrow's passing yards over his last two games
stories.summary: Burrow has thrown for 752 yards and nine touchdowns across his last two games. For the season he completes 73% of his passes for 2,115 yards, 20 touchdowns and six interceptions, with a 111.6 passer rating. Falcons coordinator Jeff Ulbrich said Burrow is playing the best football of his career.

stories.text: Bengals face the Falcons in Madrid on Sunday morning
stories.summary: Cincinnati plays Atlanta on Sunday, Nov. 8 at 9:30 a.m. ET in Madrid, Spain, shown on NFL Network. Watch how a banged-up secondary handles Atlanta's passing game while Burrow keeps the offense rolling.

teams.name: Cleveland Browns
teams.headline: Browns lose to Steelers 27-6, Watson in protocol

stories.text: Steelers sack Watson eight times in 27-6 win over Browns
stories.summary: Pittsburgh beat Cleveland 27-6 and took sole possession of first place in the AFC North, dropping the Browns to 5-3. Cleveland fumbled on its first two possessions and failed to score a touchdown for the first time this season. The Browns rushed for 34 yards.

stories.text: Deshaun Watson enters concussion protocol
stories.summary: Watson left the Steelers game after a first-quarter hit and was cleared by an outside neurotrauma consultant. On Tuesday he told the medical staff his symptoms started Monday night, and the Browns placed him in the concussion protocol. Adam Schefter reported that Shedeur Sanders is expected to start, though the team has not announced it.

stories.text: Harold Fannin Jr. posts 10 catches for 154 yards
stories.summary: The rookie tight end led Cleveland in receiving against Pittsburgh with 10 catches for 154 yards. Watson finished 27 of 39 for 324 yards with no touchdowns or interceptions. Cornerback Denzel Ward picked off Aaron Rodgers.

stories.text: 8: sacks Cleveland allowed in Pittsburgh
stories.summary: The Steelers sacked Watson eight times, and Cleveland ran for only 34 yards. The Browns went without a touchdown for the first time this season. Pittsburgh now leads the league with 26 sacks.

stories.text: Browns visit the 2-5 Saints on Sunday
stories.summary: Cleveland plays at New Orleans on Sunday, Nov. 8 at 1 p.m. ET on CBS at the Caesars Superdome. The Saints are 2-5 coming off their bye. The unofficial depth chart lists Watson as the starter with Sanders second, so watch his protocol status.

teams.name: Pittsburgh Steelers
teams.headline: Steelers lead the North heading into the bye

stories.text: Steelers hit the bye at 6-2 and atop the AFC North
stories.summary: Pittsburgh has won four straight and holds first place in the division after beating Cleveland 27-6. Aaron Rodgers called the offense incomplete but said the team is right where it wants to be. The running game and defense have carried the wins.

stories.text: Bye week opens the door for Harmon, Wilson and Pittman
stories.summary: Defensive tackle Derrick Harmon (foot) is eligible to return from injured reserve, though his timeline is unclear. Wideout Roman Wilson (hand) becomes eligible in Week 11. Michael Pittman Jr. has a foot injury and no return date, and he has played in only three games.

stories.text: Jaylen Warren owns the league's top rushing EPA
stories.summary: Warren has 704 rushing yards, sixth in the NFL, and leads the league in rushing EPA at 19.0 according to The Athletic. He ran for 143 yards and two touchdowns on 17 carries against Cleveland. Rico Dowdle added 56 yards and a score.

stories.text: 26: sacks, the most in the NFL
stories.summary: Pittsburgh leads the league with 26 sacks, including eight on Deshaun Watson. Its pressure rate of 32.6% ranks only 26th, which suggests the sack total outruns the underlying pressure.

stories.text: Steelers on bye, then a Sunday night trip to Cincinnati
stories.summary: Pittsburgh is off in Week 9. NFL.com's schedule lists the Week 10 game at the Bengals on Sunday, Nov. 15 at 8:20 p.m. ET on NBC. A Cincinnati win over Atlanta would make it a game for the division lead.

teams.name: Houston Texans
teams.headline: Texans return to Pee Wee tackling drills

stories.text: Ryans takes Texans back to Pee Wee tackling drills
stories.summary: Houston sits at 2-5 coming off its bye, and DeMeco Ryans spent the break rebuilding the defense from the ground up with basic tackling work. Will Anderson Jr. said the coaches are reteaching the group and that arm tackles do not work in this league. The Texans head to the NFL's last winless team looking to string wins together.

stories.text: Montgomery out again, Blankenship trending the same way
stories.summary: Running back David Montgomery (groin) is expected to miss his third straight game, which leaves Woody Marks as the lead back. Safety Reed Blankenship (concussion, hand) has missed five straight practices and looks unlikely to play, so M.J. Stewart would start next to Calen Bullock. Linebacker Azeez Al-Shaair and safety Jalen Pitre both practiced fully Thursday.

stories.text: Will Anderson Jr. ties T.J. Watt for the sack lead
stories.summary: Anderson has 7.5 sacks and 15 quarterback hits, a share of the league lead with T.J. Watt. Danielle Hunter adds four sacks. Houston's pass defense ranks third in dropback success rate at 41.6 percent, and it meets a Chargers line that has allowed Justin Herbert to be sacked 23 times.

stories.text: 1: interceptions C.J. Stroud has thrown in seven games
stories.summary: Stroud has one interception through seven games, and the Texans have only three giveaways all season. He ranks fourth in the NFL with 1,867 passing yards and a 100.7 passer rating. The Chargers have 17 giveaways, and Herbert leads the league with 10 interceptions.

stories.text: Texans visit winless Chargers Sunday on CBS
stories.summary: Houston plays at the Los Angeles Chargers on Sunday, Nov. 8, at 4:05 p.m. ET on CBS from SoFi Stadium. Watch whether the Texans can protect Stroud and find a ground game with Montgomery out. Their two wins this season both came on the road.

teams.name: Indianapolis Colts
teams.headline: Colts face Tuesday call on Jonathan Taylor

stories.text: Colts turn seller as the trade deadline nears
stories.summary: Indianapolis fired general manager Chris Ballard after a Week 6 loss to the Titans, then traded guard Quenton Nelson to Seattle and DeForest Buckner to San Francisco. NFL Network reports the Colts will talk trades on Jonathan Taylor, with Denver, Green Bay, Minnesota, the Giants and Seattle showing interest. Wide receiver Josh Downs has also requested a trade. The league deadline falls on Nov. 10.

stories.text: Davis-Gaither and Walley miss a second straight practice
stories.summary: Linebacker Akeem Davis-Gaither (knee) and cornerback Justin Walley (knee) did not practice Wednesday or Thursday, so their status for Dallas is unclear. Tight end Drew Ogletree (knee) went limited. Jonathan Taylor, Keenan Allen and Charvarius Ward all returned to full work Thursday. If Davis-Gaither sits, Bryce Boettcher could start beside rookie CJ Allen.

stories.text: Taylor tries to block out trade talk before Dallas
stories.summary: Jonathan Taylor has 610 rushing yards and a league-leading eight touchdowns in his seventh season with the Colts. He said he is sticking to his routine and called a possible final home game emotional. The Colts set a 4 p.m. Tuesday cutoff to decide on him, after Sunday's game.

stories.text: 30th: where the Colts defense ranks in points allowed
stories.summary: ESPN's Stephen Holder notes Indianapolis also ranks 30th in yards per play and yards per rush allowed. Over nine months the Colts have parted with Zaire Franklin, Michael Pittman Jr., Kenny Moore II, Nelson and Buckner. Holder calls the situation an obvious rebuild.

stories.text: Colts host Cowboys Sunday at 1 p.m. on Fox
stories.summary: Indianapolis (2-6) hosts the 3-5 Dallas Cowboys on Sunday, Nov. 8, at 1 p.m. ET on Fox from Lucas Oil Stadium. The Colts come off a 42-7 loss at Jacksonville. Daniel Jones will face a Dallas defense that gives up points but has talent in Caleb Downs and Quinnen Williams.

teams.name: Jacksonville Jaguars
teams.headline: Jaguars rout Ravens 33-10 on Thursday night

stories.text: Jaguars rout Ravens 33-10 and lead South by 3.5 games
stories.summary: Jacksonville beat Baltimore 33-10 in the rain on Thursday night to move to 6-2, its first Thursday night win in three seasons. The Jaguars have won five of six and lead the AFC South by three and a half games over Houston. The Ravens, without Lamar Jackson and Tyler Huntley, fell to 4-5.

stories.text: Tuten and Walker play through injuries in Baltimore
stories.summary: Running back Bhayshul Tuten (foot, ankle) and edge rusher Travon Walker (rib) were both listed questionable and both played. Tuten scored the opening touchdown on a 1-yard run. Receiver CJ Williams, cornerback Alijah Huzzie, safety Cam'Ron Silmon-Craig and end Wesley Williams were inactive.

stories.text: Lawrence throws for 242 yards and a 50-yard score
stories.summary: Trevor Lawrence completed 16 of 26 passes for 242 yards and a touchdown. His 50-yard strike to Parker Washington stretched the lead to 17-3 before halftime. Kicker Cam Little hit four field goals from 33 to 47 yards.

stories.text: 10: first-quarter points the Jaguars have allowed all year
stories.summary: That is the fewest in the NFL. The defense forced three turnovers against Baltimore, including interceptions by Montaric Brown and Jourdan Lewis, and Foye Oluokun had the lone sack. Rookie quarterback Joe Fagnano threw two interceptions.

stories.text: Jaguars visit Titans Nov. 15 in a South matchup
stories.summary: Jacksonville travels to Tennessee on Sunday, Nov. 15, at 1 p.m. ET on Fox. The Titans enter that game off a bye at 1-7. Watch whether the Jaguars keep their early-game defense and turnover edge on the road.

teams.name: Tennessee Titans
teams.headline: Titans rest at 1-7 with a 66-game streak to end

stories.text: Titans hit the bye at 1-7 after trading Jeffery Simmons
stories.summary: Tennessee sent All-Pro tackle Jeffery Simmons to Chicago on Oct. 29 for two first-round picks and a fourth-rounder. The Titans enter their bye after a 43-36 overtime loss to Cincinnati and project to pick second in the 2027 draft. Coach Robert Saleh points to a 1-5 mark in one-score games as proof his team is close.

stories.text: Carnell Tate's shoulder gets two weeks of rest
stories.summary: Rookie receiver Carnell Tate missed the Cincinnati game with a shoulder injury, and Saleh called his situation complicated for a young player. The bye gives him until the Nov. 15 game against Jacksonville. Saleh said the team will release no injury updates until required, and the offensive line was thin at the end of the loss.

stories.text: Cam Ward posts first 300-yard game in a loss
stories.summary: Ward completed 26 of 40 passes for 304 yards and two touchdowns against Cincinnati, his first 300-yard game. Tony Pollard ran for 117 yards and two scores, and Amani Hooker intercepted Joe Burrow three times. The Titans still lost in overtime.

stories.text: 66: games since the Titans last won back-to-back in a season
stories.summary: That is the longest such drought in the NFL, spanning four years. Tennessee is 7-35 since the start of 2024. Cam Ward is 4-21 as a starter.

stories.text: Bye this week, then Jaguars at Nissan Stadium Nov. 15
stories.summary: Tennessee is off in Week 9. The Titans return Sunday, Nov. 15, at 1 p.m. ET on Fox against first-place Jacksonville at Nissan Stadium. Watch how Tate and the thin offensive line look after the rest.

teams.name: Denver Broncos
teams.headline: Broncos stop Chiefs, take AFC West lead

stories.text: Broncos beat Chiefs on a goal-line stand and take first in the AFC West
stories.summary: Denver trailed 24-13 in the third quarter and won 28-24 on Nov. 1 at Empower Field, its fourth straight victory. Bo Nix threw two fourth-down touchdown passes, and Jonah Coleman scored the go-ahead run with 1:56 left. Malcolm Roach sacked Patrick Mahomes at the Denver 1 as time ran out, and the Broncos moved to 6-2 with Kansas City at 5-2.

stories.text: Three Broncos questionable for Carolina, four on injured reserve
stories.summary: Safety Brandon Jones, cornerback Kris Abrams-Draine and safety Talanoa Hufanga carry questionable tags ahead of Sunday's game. RJ Harvey, Jonah Elliss, Tyler Badie and Pat Bryant sit on injured reserve. Final designations come with the Friday report.

stories.text: Jonah Coleman delivers 104 yards and the winning touchdown
stories.summary: Coleman ran for 41 yards and caught passes for 63 against Kansas City. His 52-yard catch set up the winning score, and he finished that drive with a 5-yard run. He averages 4.5 yards per carry and played more than two thirds of Denver's snaps in Week 8.

stories.text: 9: yards Denver gained in the third quarter before the comeback
stories.summary: The Broncos managed only nine yards in the third quarter and fell behind 24-13. They then covered 80 yards on one fourth-quarter drive, and later won it with a 52-yard Nix throw to Coleman. Denver finished with 294 total yards to Kansas City's 399 and still won, with no turnovers on either side.

stories.text: Broncos visit the 3-4 Panthers on Sunday at 1 p.m. ET on CBS
stories.summary: Denver plays at Bank of America Stadium in Charlotte. Carolina ranks 28th in yards per carry allowed, which sets up another heavy dose of Coleman. The Broncos defense ranks in the top 11 in EPA per play.

teams.name: Kansas City Chiefs
teams.headline: Chiefs stew over Butker miss in Denver loss

stories.text: Reid backs Butker after the 54-yard miss that sealed the Denver loss
stories.summary: Kansas City led 24-13 in the third quarter and lost 28-24 when Harrison Butker pushed a 54-yard field goal wide right with 2:31 left. Andy Reid called criticism of the call hindsight and said the kick sat within Butker's range. He also blamed protection, saying Denver overloaded the left side and forced Butker to adjust.

stories.text: Rookie lineman Peter Woods hurt his neck in Denver
stories.summary: Woods left the Broncos game in the first half and did not return. Reid called it a stinger, and the team has not said if he will play against the Jets. Wide receiver Tyquan Thornton and running back Brashard Smith appear on the Week 9 injury list as out, though that listing should be checked against Friday's report.

stories.text: Emmett Johnson posts career-high 128 receiving yards
stories.summary: Johnson finished with 143 total yards and a touchdown against Denver. The 128 receiving yards set a personal best. Patrick Mahomes threw for 321 yards and three scores in the loss.

stories.text: 1 of 5: Butker's field goal rate from 50-plus yards this season
stories.summary: The Denver miss dropped Butker to 1 of 5 from 50 yards or longer in 2026. Since 2023 he has made 8 of 18 from that range, 44.4 percent. Through 2023 he hit 28 of 40.

stories.text: Chiefs host the 2-6 Jets on Sunday at 1 p.m. ET on CBS
stories.summary: Kansas City plays at Arrowhead Stadium. The Jets have 20 sacks to the Chiefs' nine, so pass protection is worth watching after Reid pointed to it following the Denver loss. Kenneth Walker leads Kansas City with 770 rushing yards.

teams.name: Las Vegas Raiders
teams.headline: Raiders rally past Jets, head to San Francisco

stories.text: Raiders erase a nine-point deficit to snap a four-game skid
stories.summary: Las Vegas trailed the Jets 23-14 at halftime and won 38-33 in New Jersey on Nov. 1. Kirk Cousins threw three touchdown passes and ran one in, and Dylan Laube took a kickoff back 95 yards for a score. Jeremy Chinn picked off Geno Smith in the end zone with 14 seconds left to seal it.

stories.text: Porter misses Wednesday practice, three Raiders limited
stories.summary: Cornerback Darien Porter (groin) did not practice Wednesday. Defensive tackles Thomas Booker (ankle) and Foley Fatukasi (shoulder, elbow) and tight end Ian Thomas (ankle) were limited. No game designations had been posted yet, and only the Wednesday report was available when we checked.

stories.text: Washington carries the load while Jeanty catches the ball
stories.summary: Rookie Mike Washington Jr. ran 25 times for 83 yards against the Jets. Ashton Jeanty had only two carries for 9 yards but caught three passes for 64, including a 45-yard screen that set up the go-ahead drive. Coach Klint Kubiak called the backfield a moving target and said the split will shift week to week.

stories.text: 19: Cousins' touchdown passes, second most in the NFL
stories.summary: Kirk Cousins needs two more scoring throws to pass Tom Brady's 20 for the most by a quarterback aged 38 or older in his first nine starts with a franchise since 1970. The Raiders have scored 221 points, also second in the league, but they allow 28.8 per game, 31st.

stories.text: Raiders visit the 49ers Sunday at 4:25 PM ET on FOX
stories.summary: Las Vegas plays at Levi's Stadium in its first Bay Area trip since 2018, against a 49ers team that is 6-1 after its bye. Watch a Raiders run game ranked 31st (77.3 yards per game) against the NFL's fourth-ranked defense in total yards.

teams.name: Los Angeles Chargers
teams.headline: Winless Chargers host the Texans Sunday

stories.text: Chargers fall to 0-7, the league's only winless team
stories.summary: Los Angeles lost 24-9 at the Rams in its first game after the Week 7 bye. The offense kicked three field goals and has gone nine quarters without a touchdown. Jim Harbaugh is 0-7 as a head coach for the first time.

stories.text: Derwin James stays on injured reserve until Nov. 29
stories.summary: The Chargers safety has a hamstring injury and cannot return before Nov. 29. He has played in only three games this season. Houston is also thin: receiver Jaylin Noel is out for the year with turf toe.

stories.text: Herbert has thrown an interception in every game
stories.summary: Justin Herbert threw two picks against the Rams, to Quentin Lake and Trent McDuffie, and now leads the NFL with 10. He also posted a season-best 257 passing yards in that game and has been sacked 23 times, tied for second most in the league.

stories.text: 27: drives since the Chargers last scored a touchdown
stories.summary: The Chargers have not found the end zone in nine quarters. Their last touchdown came in a 23-17 loss to Denver on Oct. 11. They are 0-4 at SoFi Stadium this season, and no team that started 0-7 or worse has made the playoffs.

stories.text: Texans visit SoFi Stadium Sunday at 4:05 PM ET on CBS
stories.summary: Houston is 2-5, coming off its bye, and favored by 4.5. Texans quarterback C.J. Stroud has 11 touchdown passes and one interception, and end Will Anderson Jr. has 7.5 sacks. The Chargers then play at Baltimore on Monday, Nov. 16 on ESPN.

teams.name: Dallas Cowboys
teams.headline: Cowboys blow a 14-point lead, lose in overtime

stories.text: Cowboys blow a 14-point lead and lose to Arizona in overtime
stories.summary: Dallas led 17-3 after three quarters and still lost 33-30 to the Cardinals. Arizona turned to Gardner Minshew, and he tied it with a touchdown pass to Michael Wilson with about a minute left. Chad Ryland, who missed the extra point, won it with a 42-yard field goal. The Cowboys sit 3-5, second in the NFC East behind the Giants.

stories.text: Ferguson and Turpin sit out Thursday as Dallas thins out
stories.summary: Tight end Jake Ferguson (ankle) and returner Kavontae Turpin (ribs) did not practice Thursday, and edge rusher Malachi Lawrence (ankle) also sat. Safeties Caleb Downs and P.J. Locke were limited after concussions and moved in the right direction. George Pickens (hamstring) and guard Tyler Smith (ankle) were limited.

stories.text: Quinnen Williams piles up two more sacks
stories.summary: The defensive tackle had two sacks against Arizona and now leads the team with five. Linebacker Shemar James picked off a pass for his first career interception, and DeMarvion Overshown forced a fumble. The Cowboys finished with five sacks and two takeaways in the loss.

stories.text: 467: Yards Arizona gained, against 261 for Dallas
stories.summary: The Cardinals outgained the Cowboys by more than 200 yards and still needed overtime to win. Dallas ran for just 2.4 yards a carry, one week after it rushed for 204 yards. Tyler Allgeier alone piled up 191 scrimmage yards.

stories.text: Cowboys visit a Colts team that has lost four straight
stories.summary: Dallas plays at Indianapolis on Sunday at 1 p.m. ET on FOX at Lucas Oil Stadium. The Colts are 2-6 and lost 42-7 at Jacksonville last week. Watch whether the Cowboys keep a lead in the fourth quarter and who is healthy in the secondary. The 49ers are next, on Nov. 15.

teams.name: New York Giants
teams.headline: Giants lead the East and head to Philadelphia

stories.text: Giants come off the bye holding first place in the NFC East
stories.summary: New York is 4-2-1 and two games ahead of Washington. Wide receiver Malik Nabers earned NFC Offensive Player of the Month for October, and cornerback Greg Newsome II signed a three-year extension through 2029. J.J. McCarthy, acquired from Minnesota on Sept. 28, has become the team's third starting quarterback this season.

stories.text: Skattebo and Carter did not practice Wednesday
stories.summary: Running back Cam Skattebo (hamstring) and outside linebacker Abdul Carter (illness) sat out the Nov. 4 practice. Tackles Jermaine Eluemunor (calf) and Andrew Thomas (groin) were limited, as was linebacker Malik Harrison (groin). Running back Tyrone Tracy Jr. is on injured reserve with a hamstring injury that GM Joe Schoen does not expect to end his season.

stories.text: Cam Skattebo runs for his first 100-yard game
stories.summary: Skattebo carried the Giants past Houston 27-21 in overtime on Oct. 25, and a 42-yard run in the extra period set up the winning score. It was the longest run of his career. He felt his hamstring afterward, so his status for Sunday is the story to watch.

stories.text: 188: Rushing yards for the Giants in the win at Houston
stories.summary: New York averaged 5.5 yards a carry in the 27-21 overtime win. Four different Giants ran for a touchdown, including Jameis Winston on a tush push. The ground game answered a challenge from coach John Harbaugh a week after the team cut Najee Harris.

stories.text: Giants face an Eagles team on a six-game skid
stories.summary: New York visits Philadelphia on Sunday, Nov. 8, at 1 p.m. ET on FOX at Lincoln Financial Field. The Eagles are 2-6 and start Joe Milton at quarterback.

teams.name: Philadelphia Eagles
teams.headline: Eagles switch to Joe Milton at quarterback

stories.text: Eagles go to Joe Milton over Tanner McKee for Week 9
stories.summary: Philadelphia will start Milton against the Giants, its third different starting quarterback this season. Coach Nick Sirianni said Monday that McKee would keep the job, and the reversal came two days later. The Eagles are 2-6, have lost six straight, and sit last in the NFC East.

stories.text: Jalen Hurts is done for the year with blood clots
stories.summary: Doctors found multiple blood clots in both of Hurts' lungs, and sources say he will miss the rest of the season. He went on injured reserve on Oct. 17. That opened the door for Milton and McKee to run the offense. A full Week 9 practice report for the rest of the roster was not available when I checked.

stories.text: Joe Milton gets his first start with limited game tape
stories.summary: Milton, 26, has five career appearances, all in relief. Last season with Dallas he went 15 of 24 for 183 yards with one touchdown and two interceptions, plus 50 rushing yards on five carries. The Eagles signed him off the Cowboys' practice squad on Oct. 16, and he has a strong arm.

stories.text: 638: Passing yards for McKee in three starts, all losses
stories.summary: McKee completed 72 of 114 passes with two touchdowns and two interceptions before the Eagles benched him. Philadelphia led Washington 10-0 on Sunday night and lost 27-10. The offense has not found a rhythm since Hurts went down.

stories.text: Eagles host the first-place Giants on Sunday
stories.summary: Philadelphia hosts New York on Sunday, Nov. 8, at 1 p.m. ET on FOX at Lincoln Financial Field. The Giants are 4-2-1 and lead the division. Watch how Milton handles the pass rush and whether the Eagles can run the ball, after they managed only 91 rushing yards against Washington.

teams.name: Washington Commanders
teams.headline: Commanders end the skid with 27 straight points

stories.text: Commanders erase a 10-0 deficit and beat the Eagles 27-10
stories.summary: Washington scored 27 unanswered points on Sunday night for its first win in more than a month. The defense sacked Tanner McKee five times and intercepted him once. The Commanders are 2-4-1 and sit two games behind the first-place Giants.

stories.text: Burks sits with a foot injury, Daniels practices fully
stories.summary: Wide receiver Treylon Burks (foot) did not practice Wednesday or Thursday. Tight end John Bates (shoulder), guard Sam Cosmi (knee) and tackle Shy Tuttle (shoulder) were limited both days. Quarterback Jayden Daniels (left elbow) was a full participant both days.

stories.text: Jayden Daniels steadies the offense after a slow start
stories.summary: Daniels went 16 of 29 for 217 yards and a touchdown against Philadelphia, with no interceptions and 23 rushing yards. He found new targets with Terry McLaurin out, and Treylon Burks led the team in receiving yards with a 53-yard catch in the third quarter.

stories.text: 46.5%: Share of McKee's dropbacks the Commanders pressured
stories.summary: Washington's defensive line shut Philadelphia out for three quarters. Odafe Oweh, Shy Tuttle and Charles Omenihu each recorded a sack, and Dorance Armstrong forced a fumble that Omenihu recovered.

stories.text: Commanders host the Rams at Northwest Stadium
stories.summary: Washington hosts Los Angeles on Sunday, Nov. 8, at 1 p.m. ET. The Rams are 4-4 and beat the Chargers 24-9 last week, with Puka Nacua catching 11 passes. Watch the Commanders' pass rush against Matthew Stafford.

teams.name: Chicago Bears
teams.headline: Bears roll Seattle, host Tampa Bay on Sunday night

stories.text: Bears beat Seattle 34-17 for a third straight win
stories.summary: Chicago handled the defending champions on Monday Night Football and moved to 6-2. The Bears led 13-9 at the half, then scored 14 points in the fourth quarter to pull away. Tampa Bay comes to Soldier Field next, and both teams sit a half-game back in their divisions.

stories.text: Monangai, Jackson and Thuney sit out Thursday practice
stories.summary: Running back Kyle Monangai (thumb and toe), linebacker D'Marco Jackson (ankle) and guard Joe Thuney (listed as a rest day) did not practice Thursday. Tackle Theo Benedet (shoulder) and lineman Grady Jarrett (groin) both moved up from no practice to limited. Running back Zavier Scott went on injured reserve.

stories.text: Swift scores three rushing touchdowns against Seattle
stories.summary: D'Andre Swift ran for three scores and 69 yards in the win over the Seahawks. He now has 545 rushing yards on 143 carries and 10 touchdowns this season. Caleb Williams threw the Bears' only first-half touchdown, a short pass to Luther Burden III.

stories.text: 23.8%: Bears lead the NFL in third-down defense
stories.summary: Opponents convert only 23.8 percent of their third downs against Chicago, the best mark in the league. The defense also ranks seventh in yards allowed (305.8 per game) and eighth in points allowed (20.0). The offense ranks third in total yards at 387.3 per game.

stories.text: Tampa Bay at Soldier Field on Sunday Night Football
stories.summary: The Bears host the 3-5 Buccaneers on Sunday, Nov. 8 at 8:20 p.m. ET on NBC. Tampa Bay has won two straight, including a game against Atlanta where it ran for 324 yards. Watch how Chicago's run defense answers that ground game.

teams.name: Detroit Lions
teams.headline: Lions run past Vikings, wait on Jack Campbell

stories.text: Lions run over Minnesota 19-15 on the ground
stories.summary: Detroit beat the previously unbeaten Vikings at Ford Field and outgained them 384 yards to 266. The Lions piled up 230 rushing yards and held the ball for 35:43. Jahmyr Gibbs carried 23 times for 153 yards and a touchdown.

stories.text: Jack Campbell still in hospital with a neck injury
stories.summary: The All-Pro linebacker got hurt in the fourth quarter against Minnesota and left on a cart. He has full movement in his lower body and is progressing with his upper body. Edge rusher DJ Wonnum, cornerback DJ Reed and center Cade Mays are all questionable for Miami.

stories.text: Gibbs piles up 153 yards on 23 carries
stories.summary: Jahmyr Gibbs carried the Detroit offense against Minnesota with 153 yards and a touchdown. Jameson Williams added four catches for 70 yards and a score. Jared Goff has thrown a touchdown pass in 30 straight games.

stories.text: 230: rushing yards for Detroit against Minnesota
stories.summary: The Lions ran for 230 yards while the Vikings managed 81. Detroit passed for only 154 yards and still won the yardage battle by 118. The Lions turned the ball over once, the same as Minnesota.

stories.text: Lions visit the 1-6 Dolphins on Sunday
stories.summary: Detroit plays at Miami on Sunday, Nov. 8 at 1 p.m. ET and goes for a fourth straight win. The Lions own the NFL's top offense at 395.4 yards per game. This is the first meeting between the teams since 2022, and Jeff Hafley's young Dolphins start eight rookies.

teams.name: Green Bay Packers
teams.headline: Packers beat Carolina, head to New England

stories.text: Packers beat Carolina 27-19 on Thursday night
stories.summary: Green Bay moved to 5-3 at Lambeau Field despite three turnovers, including a fumble on the opening kickoff. The defense sacked Bryce Young six times and sealed the game with a late sack by Dani Dennis-Sutton. The Packers have held their last five opponents to 20 points or fewer.

stories.text: Watson limited with broken rib; Parsons not yet back
stories.summary: Receiver Christian Watson broke a rib against Carolina but practiced in a limited role Wednesday and Thursday, and he is likely to play. Edge rusher Micah Parsons is ramping up in practice but will not play Sunday, with Week 12 the likeliest return. Running back MarShawn Lloyd (knee) and cornerback Keisean Nixon (groin) are also on the report.

stories.text: Love throws three touchdowns in the win over Carolina
stories.summary: Jordan Love went 30-of-41 for 288 yards and three scores to Tucker Kraft, Matthew Golden and Josh Jacobs. He also threw an interception in the end zone. Watson caught eight passes for 113 yards.

stories.text: 6: sacks of Bryce Young in Green Bay's win
stories.summary: The Packers dropped Carolina's quarterback six times on Thursday night. Young still threw for 209 yards and a touchdown, but the pressure kept the Panthers from closing the gap until late. Green Bay's defense has not allowed more than 20 points in five straight games.

stories.text: Packers visit Patriots on Sunday afternoon
stories.summary: Green Bay plays at New England on Sunday, Nov. 8 at 4:25 p.m. ET on FOX. The Patriots could be without receiver A.J. Brown, running back TreVeyon Henderson, tight end Hunter Henry and cornerback Marcus Jones, all on their injury list. Watch who replaces Nixon if the cornerback sits.

teams.name: Minnesota Vikings
teams.headline: Wentz starts Monday as Murray sits with hamstring

stories.text: Wentz replaces Murray for Monday night vs. Buffalo
stories.summary: Coach Kevin O'Connell ruled quarterback Kyler Murray out with a hamstring strain and called it week to week. Carson Wentz starts against the Bills, with Max Brosmer as the backup. Minnesota would rather rest Murray now than risk a bigger injury to a mobile quarterback.

stories.text: Murray out; Jackson sits, Darrisaw expected to practice
stories.summary: Murray's hamstring strain is the headline, and he had played every snap in Minnesota's previous five games. Safety Theo Jackson (quad) missed Thursday's practice. Left tackle Christian Darrisaw is expected to practice.

stories.text: Van Ginkel records 2.5 sacks in a losing effort
stories.summary: Andrew Van Ginkel finished with 2.5 sacks and four tackles in the 19-15 loss at Detroit. Murray went 17-of-29 for 210 yards and two touchdowns in that game. The Vikings fell to 6-1 after the loss.

stories.text: 30th: Vikings offense ranks in EPA per play
stories.summary: Minnesota's offense sits 30th in the league in EPA per play. The defense ranks second in both EPA per play and success rate, which explains how a 6-1 team runs such a lopsided profile. Wentz has thrown 276 yards and three touchdowns without an interception this season.

stories.text: Bills at U.S. Bank Stadium on Monday Night Football
stories.summary: Minnesota hosts Buffalo on Monday, Nov. 9 at 8:15 p.m. ET on ABC. Wentz makes the start, so watch how O'Connell shapes the game plan around him and a defense built on pressure.

teams.name: Atlanta Falcons
teams.headline: Falcons fly to Madrid after a shutout loss

stories.text: Falcons carry a 16-0 loss across the Atlantic
stories.summary: Atlanta lost 16-0 at Tampa Bay on Nov. 1 and now travels to Madrid to face Cincinnati. Michael Penix Jr. went 8 of 24 for 125 yards, and Bijan Robinson managed 76 yards on 19 carries. Coach Kevin Stefanski has to reset an offense that never scored.

stories.text: Robinson and Deablo limited, Branch out in Madrid
stories.summary: Running back Brian Robinson Jr. (hamstring) was limited Wednesday and Thursday. Linebackers Divine Deablo (forearm) and Yasir Abdullah (hamstring) were also limited. Receiver Zachariah Branch is out with a hamstring injury, and Samson Ebukam, who hurt his hamstring in the Tampa loss, went on injured reserve.

stories.text: James Pearce Jr. returns from suspension
stories.summary: Pearce rejoined the walkthrough after missing the first eight games on suspension. Stefanski said the staff will decide his snap count this week. He was a full participant Wednesday and could add pass rush to a defense that lost Ebukam.

stories.text: 4: interceptions Penix threw against Tampa Bay
stories.summary: The Buccaneers picked off Penix four times, and he finished with 125 passing yards on 24 attempts. Linebacker Alex Anzalone took two of them in the first quarter. Atlanta never reached the end zone.

stories.text: Bengals in Madrid, Sunday at 9:30 a.m. ET
stories.summary: Atlanta plays Cincinnati at Bernabeu Stadium in Madrid on Sunday, Nov. 8, with kickoff at 9:30 a.m. ET on NFL Network. Watch whether Robinson and Pearce play and whether the offense finds points after the shutout.

teams.name: Carolina Panthers
teams.headline: Panthers hold first place despite two straight losses

stories.text: Young's ankle and the sack problem top Carolina's week
stories.summary: Bryce Young's injury listing changed from a knee to an ankle, and he practiced fully. Carolina has lost two straight, most recently 27-19 at Green Bay, where Young took six sacks. The Panthers still lead a tight NFC South at 3-4.

stories.text: Phillips, Lee, Okereke and Lewis sit out Thursday
stories.summary: Outside linebacker Jaelan Phillips (hamstring), cornerback Will Lee III (hamstring), linebacker Bobby Okereke (foot) and guard Damien Lewis (knee) did not practice Thursday. Young practiced in full with the ankle. Guard Corey Bullock and tackle Torricelli Simpkins III moved up to full.

stories.text: McMillan leads the Panthers with 569 yards
stories.summary: Receiver Tetairoa McMillan has 42 catches for 569 yards, tops on the team. He becomes Young's main target against a Denver defense that pressures the quarterback. Carolina needs him to win early downs.

stories.text: 11: sacks Carolina allowed in its last two games
stories.summary: The Panthers gave up 11 sacks across their past two games, including six on Young at Green Bay. Denver arrives at 6-2 with a pass rush the line must handle. Protection decides this game.

stories.text: Broncos visit Sunday at 1 p.m. ET on CBS
stories.summary: Carolina hosts Denver on Sunday, Nov. 8, at 1 p.m. ET on CBS. The Broncos are 6-2. Watch the Panthers' offensive line and the status of Phillips and Lee.

teams.name: New Orleans Saints
teams.headline: Saints cut kicker Carlson, hunt for points

stories.text: Saints release Carlson and search for a kicker
stories.summary: New Orleans released kicker Daniel Carlson after he made 8 of 12 field goals. Practice-squad kicker Charlie Smyth looks like the likeliest replacement, and Kellen Moore does not plan to add other kickers this week. The Saints are 2-5 after their bye.

stories.text: Donaldson out of practice, Kamara limited
stories.summary: Running back CJ Donaldson (shoulder, concussion) did not practice Thursday. Alvin Kamara returned as limited after a rest and back designation. Receiver Jordyn Tyson (hamstring), tackle Kelvin Banks Jr. (ankle) and cornerback Martin Emerson Jr. (shin) were limited.

stories.text: Chase Young leads the Saints with 7 sacks
stories.summary: Young leads New Orleans with 7 sacks, and Carl Granderson has 5.5. They give the Saints their best chance to pressure Deshaun Watson on Sunday.

stories.text: 86: rushing yards per game, 30th in the NFL
stories.summary: The Saints average 86 rushing yards and 3.5 yards per carry, and no player has a 100-yard game. Kendre Miller leads with 159 yards, and Travis Etienne Jr. is on injured reserve. Moore says he will spend a lot of time on how to score.

stories.text: Browns at the Superdome, Sunday at 1 p.m. ET
stories.summary: New Orleans hosts Cleveland on Sunday, Nov. 8, at noon CT (1 p.m. ET) on CBS. The Browns are 5-3. The Saints have won the last three meetings.

teams.name: Tampa Bay Buccaneers
teams.headline: Bucs run for a franchise record, now visit Chicago

stories.text: Bucs shut out Atlanta on the ground, 16-0
stories.summary: Tampa Bay beat Atlanta 16-0 in the rain and set a franchise single-game rushing record. Bucky Irving ran for 170 yards and the only touchdown, and Kenny Gainwell added 140. Baker Mayfield went 0 for 3 without a completion.

stories.text: Diaby and Egbuka miss Wednesday practice
stories.summary: Edge rusher Yaya Diaby (knee) and receiver Emeka Egbuka (foot) did not practice Wednesday. Running back Kenneth Gainwell (hip) and safety Tykee Smith (ankle) were limited. Mayfield (right thumb) practiced in full.

stories.text: Anzalone picks off Penix twice in the first quarter
stories.summary: Linebacker Alex Anzalone had six tackles and two interceptions against Atlanta, both in the first quarter. He now has three interceptions this season. Tampa Bay picked off Michael Penix Jr. four times in total.

stories.text: 0: completed passes in a Bucs win over Atlanta
stories.summary: Mayfield threw three passes and completed none, and the Bucs still won. Irving and Gainwell carried the offense for 310 combined rushing yards. Tampa Bay ranks first in rushing offense and second in rushing defense.

stories.text: Bears on Sunday Night Football, 8:20 p.m. ET
stories.summary: Tampa Bay visits Chicago at Soldier Field on Sunday, Nov. 8, at 8:20 p.m. ET on Sunday Night Football. The Bears are 6-2, and Caleb Williams has 1,267 passing yards. Watch whether the run game keeps working against a stronger opponent.

teams.name: Arizona Cardinals
teams.headline: Minshew gets the start at Seattle

stories.text: Cardinals hand the offense to Gardner Minshew
stories.summary: Coach Mike LaFleur named Gardner Minshew the starter for Sunday in Seattle after Jacoby Brissett went 10 of 23 for 117 yards and an interception in Dallas. Minshew took over in the third quarter, led four straight touchdown drives and finished with three touchdown passes in a 33-30 overtime win. Brissett moves to emergency third quarterback and rookie Carson Beck becomes the backup.

stories.text: Jeremiyah Love goes to IR with a high ankle sprain
stories.summary: The rookie running back left the Dallas game in the first half and now sits on injured reserve for at least four weeks, with a reported timeline of four to five. LaFleur said the sprain involves a different part of the ankle than his earlier injuries. Love had 268 rushing yards and one touchdown in six games. Bam Knight also left the Dallas game and did not practice Wednesday.

stories.text: Tyler Allgeier runs wild with the backfield thinned
stories.summary: Allgeier stepped in after Love and Knight went down and ran for 147 yards on 11 carries, including a 63-yard touchdown shortly after Minshew entered. He scored twice and piled up 191 scrimmage yards. With Love on IR, he is now the lead back.

stories.text: 4: straight touchdown drives after Minshew checked in
stories.summary: Arizona trailed 17-3 in the third quarter and was down 27-17 with 3:54 left. Minshew went 17 of 23 for 188 yards and three scores, hitting Michael Wilson with six seconds left in regulation to force overtime. The defense piled up four sacks, including one from Josh Sweat in overtime.

stories.text: Cardinals visit Seahawks Sunday on FOX
stories.summary: Arizona plays at Seattle on Sunday, Nov. 8 at 4:25 p.m. ET on FOX. Seattle won the first meeting 31-7. Watch whether Minshew can keep the offense moving with Love out and several linemen and Budda Baker missing Wednesday practice, and whether the pass rush can hit a Seahawks team without Sam Darnold.

teams.name: Los Angeles Rams
teams.headline: Rams win two straight, head to Washington

stories.text: Rams beat the Chargers 24-9 for a second straight win
stories.summary: Los Angeles held Justin Herbert to a season-low downfield pass rate and pulled even at 4-4 with a 24-9 win at SoFi Stadium. Trent McDuffie intercepted Herbert's only second-half downfield throw. Matthew Stafford was pressured on 5 of his first 11 dropbacks, then on just 1 of his final 15.

stories.text: Jaylen Watson needs shoulder surgery, done for 2026
stories.summary: The cornerback goes on season-ending injured reserve. Myles Garrett (knee) and tight end Terrance Ferguson (ankle) opened their 21-day practice windows as limited participants Wednesday, and running back Ronnie Rivers returns from IR. Trent McDuffie did not practice but came in feeling better than expected, according to McVay. Josh Wallace and Emmanuel Forbes Jr. take on more work at corner.

stories.text: Stafford wins the quick game against the Chargers
stories.summary: Stafford averaged 2.38 seconds to throw against the Chargers, his third-quickest game since joining the Rams in 2021. On passes released in under 2.5 seconds he went 13 of 14 for 94 yards and a touchdown. Blake Corum added 6.6 yards per carry in the win.

stories.text: 369: Puka Nacua's receptions through 50 career games
stories.summary: That total is 23 more than any other player in NFL history through 50 games. Nacua also has 4,756 receiving yards in that span, second only to Justin Jefferson's 4,825, and passed Lance Alworth for second place.

stories.text: Rams visit Commanders Sunday at 1 p.m. ET on FOX
stories.summary: Los Angeles plays at Northwest Stadium in Landover, Maryland, on Sunday, Nov. 8 at 1 p.m. ET (10 a.m. PT) on FOX, going for a third straight win. Washington is 2-4-1, lost receiver Terry McLaurin to a torn patellar tendon, and relies on Jayden Daniels' legs, so the Rams' edge discipline gets a test.

teams.name: San Francisco 49ers
teams.headline: 49ers return from bye with WRs hurting

stories.text: 49ers come off the bye at 6-1 with receivers missing
stories.summary: San Francisco hosts the Raiders after a bye that followed a loss to Atlanta. The 49ers rank sixth in total offense at 371.4 yards per game and fourth in scoring at 28.1 points, but Mike Evans, Deebo Samuel and Christian McCaffrey all missed Wednesday practice.

stories.text: Evans, Samuel and McCaffrey sit out Wednesday practice
stories.summary: Kyle Shanahan said he would be surprised if Samuel (hamstring) plays Sunday, and Evans (ribs, Achilles) is trending the right direction but not ready to ramp up. McCaffrey's hamstring is less serious, and Shanahan hoped to see him limited Thursday. Nick Bosa (knee, calf) was limited and Siran Neal did not practice.

stories.text: George Kittle leads a thinned receiving group
stories.summary: Kittle leads the 49ers with 34 catches for 425 yards and five touchdowns, a 12.5-yard average. With the wide receivers banged up, the tight end carries more of the passing offense. Christian McCaffrey leads the ground game with 389 yards and eight touchdowns on 84 carries.

stories.text: 56.4%: Brock Purdy's passing success rate leads the NFL
stories.summary: Purdy completes 69.2 percent of his throws with 15 touchdowns and a 110.1 passer rating, top five in completion rate and touchdown passes. Evans and Samuel account for six of those 15 touchdown passes, which puts extra weight on their health.

stories.text: Raiders visit Levi's Stadium Sunday on FOX
stories.summary: San Francisco hosts Las Vegas on Sunday, Nov. 8 at 4:25 p.m. ET (1:25 p.m. PT) on FOX. The Raiders are 4-4 and rank 31st in rushing offense and 30th in rush defense, which sets up McCaffrey if he plays. Quarterback Kirk Cousins has 19 touchdown passes, second in the league.

teams.name: Seattle Seahawks
teams.headline: Darnold out vs Cardinals with quad injury

stories.text: Sam Darnold is out Sunday with a quad injury
stories.summary: Mike Macdonald ruled out his starting quarterback Wednesday. Darnold hurt the quad late in the 34-17 Monday night loss to Chicago and also cracked a rib on the second play of that game. He is week to week, will not go on injured reserve, and could return at Las Vegas.

stories.text: Drew Lock's elbow clouds the Seattle QB plan
stories.summary: Lock is the planned starter but has a right elbow injury that limits his throwing in practice, so Jalen Milroe takes first-team reps as insurance. Seattle signed Adrian Martinez to the practice squad. Charles Cross (ankle), Rashid Shaheed (knee) and Leonard Williams (stinger) are not ruled out.

stories.text: Jaxon Smith-Njigba keeps piling up yards in a loss
stories.summary: He caught six passes for 118 yards and a touchdown against Chicago, his seventh 100-yard game in eight weeks. He passed Joey Galloway for eighth on Seattle's career receiving list. Cooper Kupp caught just one pass, a 7-yard touchdown.

stories.text: 985: Smith-Njigba's receiving yards through eight games
stories.summary: That mark is the second-most through eight games in the Super Bowl era, behind Tyreek Hill's 1,014 in 2023, and it leads the NFL by 259 yards. Seattle also converted just 1 of 11 third downs against the Bears.

stories.text: Seahawks host Cardinals Sunday on FOX
stories.summary: Seattle plays Arizona on Sunday, Nov. 8 at 4:25 p.m. ET on FOX at Lumen Field. After that the Seahawks go to Las Vegas, take their bye, then visit San Francisco on the final Sunday of November. Watch the quarterback situation and whether Jadarian Price keeps getting snaps over Zach Charbonnet.
